lines: Pitch and envelope follower: analyses an incoming sound in real time and puts out the pitch it finds as 1V/oct, along with an envelope tracking the level of the sound
The sound to be analysed
The detected fundamental of the incoming sound, as 1V/oct pitch
Filters high frequencies out of the incoming sound before it is analysed, so that sibilants such as ss and ff are not detected as very high notes
Smooths the pitch output, taking out spikes and turning a step between two notes into a slide
Smooths the envelope output, taking out spikes and giving the level a fade-in and a fade-out
Sets the level of the envelope output, and with it the height of the envelope drawn on the panel
The envelope, following the level of the incoming sound
Note — the pitch display gives the note name and cents, the frequency, the output voltage, and the detection latency in milliseconds, which is shorter for higher notes
Note — the module has nothing to follow until a sound is patched into its audio input; neither output moves on its own
Follower.notes: Version 2.4.1 added polyphonic cable support to Follower; how the channels are handled is not stated anywhere, so no line covers it.

lines: Play-only drum trigger sequencer: plays up to 25 named phrases of drum notes across ten voices, built in Entrian Drummer and saved for the free plugin
The clock that drives playback, at four ticks per beat, which a clock module calls x4 or 1/16th
Chooses which of the 25 phrases plays, C3 selecting the first and the 25 semitones up to C5 the last; set to trigger on the menu it steps to the next non-empty phrase or picks one at random
A trigger returning the playhead to the beginning, or to the start repeat marker with that option set on the menu; playback carries on immediately if the sequencer is running
A trigger toggling between running and stopped; while stopped the gates are closed and clock ticks are ignored
Returns the playhead to the beginning, or to the start repeat marker with that option set on the menu
Starts and stops playback
A trigger on each note played by that voice
A trigger on each note of that voice that is marked as an accent in the editor
The velocity of the note being played by that voice
A trigger each time the playhead reaches the end of the phrase
Carries a reset out of the sequencer each time its Reset button is pressed, on the panel or in the editor window, so a clock module can be reset from here
Carries the Run button out of the sequencer, pressed on the panel or in the editor window, so a clock module can be started and stopped from here
Note — the module is empty when it is added. It plays a patch saved out of Entrian Sequencers, or a MIDI file imported into the editor window, and until one of those arrives there is nothing to play
Note — clicking the large display opens an editor window showing the notes. They cannot be recorded here, but a MIDI file can be imported into that window or dropped onto it
Note — the playhead and the start and end repeat markers are drawn on the large display and can be moved by clicking and dragging there, without opening the editor window
Note — the small display names the phrase now playing, and clicking it lists the 25 phrases to choose from
Note — the Phrase CV/menu control in the editor window, not the panel menu, sets when a change of phrase takes effect: Instant at once, or End of phrase at the end of the current one
Menu — Phrase selection input: — how the phrase input is read: Pitch, C3-C5; Trigger next non-empty phrase; Trigger random phrase (random but fair); or Trigger random phrase (truly random)
Menu — Shared playhead: — Don't share the playhead, Shared playhead leader or Shared playhead follower, which moves the playheads of all the linked Entrian sequencers together
Menu — Delay Clock/Reset/Run inputs — delays those three inputs by a whole number of samples, to offset the one-sample delay every Rack cable adds; Auto is the default and None the other choice
Menu — Set playhead to start marker on reset — a reset sends the playhead to the start repeat marker instead of to the beginning
Menu — Save patch to use Entrian Sequencers... — writes the patch out again with each Player module swapped for the Entrian Sequencers module it came from
Player-Drummer.notes: The Reset and Run outputs (indices 30 and 31) are described from the maker's release notes, which say the editor's Run and Reset buttons have matching outputs on the panel for driving your clock. Whether Run is a gate or a trigger is not stated anywhere and was not read out of the binary, so neither jack is given a family. The End of phrase output on Drummer and Melody, and End of clip on Timeline, are named in the release notes and nowhere else; End of clip is left untagged because which track's clip it follows is not stated. The panel menu also carries Stop recording at end of song and Automatically add repeat markers when recording, which are recording options a play-only module cannot use, and Light theme and Dark theme, which are cosmetic. None of those gets a line.

notes: Menu item names read out of the 2.4.1 binary's appendContextMenu code. The selection-input label is built at runtime from the module's own word plus ' selection input:', so it prints as Phrase selection input: on Drummer and Melody and Song selection input: on Timeline; somebody should confirm the capital. The CV/menu control with its Instant and End of phrase choices sits among the editor window's controls in the binary, not in appendContextMenu, so its line says the editor window. Light theme and Dark theme are on every module in the plugin and are cosmetic, so they get no line anywhere, Follower included.
